I would say I'm a new hobbyist when it comes to car detailing. My local detailer told me he only uses ardex products and I love how my tires have been looking. The only thing is I can't really find their products anywhere. I believe it may be ardex "new concept tire dressing". Found it on amazon and a couple of other sites, but not much detail and not sure what a good price is.

If you're familiar with it, whats a decent price .. how should it be applied?

To be honest, it looks over priced on Amazon. For the best bang for your buck use Meguiar's Endurance Gel. It's really shiny though. I've also used Chemical Guys VRP dressing, this isn't bad and isn't much more than Meguiar's. You'll want to pick up an applicator to put this stuff on and spread it evenly. You should be able to find these cheap at a local automotive store.
Thanks man. Awesome informative reply. I've used this product from Meguiar's Hot Shine and the sling off was pretty bad. Any comparison with the products you listed?

I think sling really depends on how you apply the products. I have yet to come across one that won't sling if you slather it all over the sidewall and drive right away. My recommendation is to apply the tire dressing at the end of the day and let it sit overnight. You shouldn't have any sling the following day. If you need to apply it then drive, put on a light coat and re-apply later when your car will sit idle.

There are several games that were originally manufactured for the Famicom, and were fitted with an adapter to be sold in the US and played on the NES. Using this adapter, you can play Famicom games on your NES. Here are the games that are known to contain this converter:

  • 1942
  • Clu Clu Land
  • Donkey Kong Jr.
  • Duck Hunt
  • Elevator Action
  • Excitebike
  • Golf
  • Gumshoe
  • Gyromite
  • Hogan’s Alley
  • Mike Tyson’s Punch-Out!!
  • Pinball
  • Raid on Bungeling Bay
  • Rygar
  • Soccer
  • Stack Up
  • Tennis
  • Urban Champion
  • Wizards and Warriors
  • Wrecking Crew

I found mine inside of a Gyromite cart. I ended up sacrificing a broken NES game to create my own homemade adapter cartridge. I can provide pics if you guys want.

Anyway, to identify whether or not the above listed games contain the adapter, you can look at a few things without even opening the cartridge. First, look at the number of screws on the back. Five screw carts may contain the adapter, three screw carts will not. Next, look at the pins on the cartridge connector. On a regular NES game, the pins are centered, on the adapter cart, they are not.

Here is the adapter placed into a broken NES cart for permanent use. Front, back, top, cartridge pins.
